newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Pilkington outlook brighter after H1.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Pilkington outlook brighter after H1.

text.p: British glassmaker Pilkington Plc said on Thursday half-year profits were hit by tough trading conditions in Europe, but it was slightly more optimistic about its prospects in the second half of the year.
Pre-tax profits slipped to 75 million pounds ($121.7 million) after an exceptional charge of seven million pounds on the sale of the Barnes-Hind contact lens business.
The profit figure compares with 104 million previously, and was at the low end of market expectations. But Pilkington maintained its interim dividend at 1.75p.

"Both prices and volumes strengthened towards the end of September and during October, and our businesses elsewhere, particularly in North and South America, continue to perform well," said Chairman Nigel Rudd in a statement.
"Against this background, we would expect to see an improving trend in the second half of the year."
Pilkington said the rapid decline in prices of standard clear glass in the second half of last year and the first quarter of the current year was the principal reason for the profit decline.
However, the equity market took Pilkington's results in stride, marking its shares 2-1/2p higher to 172p on the back of the company's upbeat statement.
"The negative comments on Europe were expected, and it seems to be turning...things seem to be firming up, and the outlook looks good," said one sector analyst.

Andrew Robb, group finance director of Pilkington, told Reuters the benefits of its restructuring charge, which knocked 155 million pounds off its previous annual pre-tax profits and cost 1,900 jobs, was beginning to come through.

"In the first half, we had cost savings of 35 million pounds, which includes the first part of the savings coming out of the restructuring programme. But they will accelerate as we get our plants reorganised in Europe," said Robb.
Pilkington said its underlying strategy was still to emphasise new product development, increase downstream processing, cost reduction and cash generation.

"Strategy is two pronged. One is the continuing attention to improving the margins in our mature businesses, particularly in Europe. The other is expanding in the new areas like South America, China and probably India as well," said Robb. ($1=.6165 Pound)
